correctness.rationale: At r=2 and alpha<d, v_next<=q v with 0<q<1. Exact scalar restriction f(z)=(1+z)e^(-2z)-1 has f²(z)=z-(4/3)z³+(8/15)z⁵+(4/9)z⁶+O(z⁷). Small-data trapping and summable exponential forcing imply z_n->0. A local inverse of f with Lipschitz L and Lq<1 constructs an exponentially close unique scalar orbit. By the strong-stable theorem, the zero scalar phase is a smooth invariant curve; the degree-two invariance equation gives the explicit h1 and h2, with strictly negative derivative of h2 in k. Nonzero scalar phase has inverse-square even-return increment 8/3+64/(15w)+O(w^(-3/2)), whose absolutely summable renormalized remainder yields (8/3)n+(8/5)log n+C+o(1). Exponential shadowing transports the clock unchanged. Symbolic and finite diagnostic checker VERIFY_OK was freshly run from the attached package source; numerical evidence is not the proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2023 ecological map has a natural boundary eigenvalue -1 at r=2, where linear eigenvalues alone do not determine convergence. The new result identifies a unique local fast-decay separatrix, computes its first nontrivial fear-sensitive curvature and proves a fully renormalized universal critical relaxation law on both relative open sides. The strict-mortality case differs substantively from already studied double-neutral algebraic predator recovery. Unlike a scalar Ricker normalization, the result handles genuine nonzero predator initial states and nonlinear fear/predation forcing. Global basins, generic parabolic theory and independent priority are not claimed.
